config.title: Zustand Persist Middleware

intro.title: Zustand Persist Middleware
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple counter app that saves its count value between browser sessions using Zustand's persist middleware. You will learn how to use the persist middleware to automatically store and retrieve state from localStorage. The main technologies involved are React, Zustand for state management, and the persist middleware. By the end, you will understand how to make your app's state persistent, enhancing the user experience.
intro.usecase: Zustand's persist middleware is essential for maintaining user preferences and application state across sessions in real-world applications. In e-commerce platforms, it preserves shopping cart items and user-selected filters even after browser refreshes or accidental tab closures. Dashboard applications use it to remember customized widget layouts, chart configurations, and user-selected date ranges. Form-heavy applications like CRM systems benefit by persisting partially completed forms, preventing data loss during interruptions.

objectives: Initialize a Zustand store with the persist middleware
Configure persistence options for a Zustand store
Apply the persist middleware to maintain state across page reloads
Manipulate persisted state values through store actions
Integrate persisted state with React components
Control when and how state persistence occurs
Update existing Zustand stores to include persistence

steps.title: Import React and createStore from zustand
steps.instruction: Import React and the create function from zustand. Use the named import 'create' from 'zustand'.
steps.hint: You'll need two import statements: one for React and one for zustand's create function.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and create from zustand here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to start building a Zustand store.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react' and create is imported from 'zustand'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both React from 'react' and the create function from 'zustand'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the imports. You need to import React from 'react' and the create function from 'zustand'.

steps.title: Create a basic Zustand store without persistence
steps.instruction: Create a basic counter store using Zustand's create function. Define a store with count state and increment/decrement actions.
steps.hint: Use the create function to define a store with an initial state and actions that update that state.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zustand store is created with count state and increment/decrement actions, ready to be used in components.
successCriteria: A store named useCounterStore is created with count state initialized to 0, and increment and decrement actions that update the count.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your store includes count state, increment, and decrement actions.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store wasn't created correctly. Check that you're using create from zustand and defining all required properties.

steps.title: Import persist middleware from zustand/middleware
steps.hint: Add an import statement for persist from the zustand/middleware package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing a middleware
import { persist } from 'zustand/middleware';
steps.expectedOutcome: The persist middleware is imported and available for use in the store.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the persist middleware.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing persist from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The persist middleware import is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Wrap the store with persist middleware
steps.instruction: Wrap your existing store configuration with the persist() function imported from 'zustand/middleware'.
steps.hint: Call persist() and pass your store configuration function as its first argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store configuration is now wrapped with persist(), making it ready for persistence configuration.
successCriteria: The create() call now has persist() wrapping the store configuration function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure persist() is called and wraps the entire store configuration function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The store configuration isn't properly wrapped with persist(). Check that persist() is called with your configuration function as its first argument.

steps.title: Configure persistence options (name and storage)
steps.instruction: Add a name and getStorage configuration to the persist middleware call in your store.
steps.hint: Pass a configuration object as the second argument to persist. Include a 'name' property (string) and a 'getStorage' function that returns localStorage.
steps.expectedOutcome: The persist middleware now has a configuration object with name and getStorage properties, enabling persistence with a specific key and localStorage.
successCriteria: The persist call includes a configuration object with a 'name' property (string) and a 'getStorage' function that returns localStorage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some configuration, but make sure both 'name' (a string) and 'getStorage' (a function returning localStorage) are present.
steps.feedbackWrong: The persist configuration is missing or incorrect. Add a configuration object with 'name' and 'getStorage' properties.

steps.title: Create a React component to use the store
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Counter that returns a JSX wrapper element (like a div).
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name Counter. Inside, return a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Counter component is defined and returns a div element.
successCriteria: The Counter component is defined (as a function or arrow function) and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the Counter component returns a JSX element (like a div).
steps.feedbackWrong: The Counter component isn't defined correctly. Create a functional component named Counter that returns a div element.

steps.title: Access store state and actions in the component
steps.instruction: Inside your Counter component, use the useCounterStore hook to access the count state and increment action.
steps.hint: Call useCounterStore() and destructure the count and increment values from the returned object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to the store's count value and increment function.
successCriteria: The useCounterStore hook is called and destructured to get count and increment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useCounterStore() and destructuring both count and increment.
steps.feedbackWrong: call useCounterStore() and destructure the count and increment values.

steps.title: Display the current count value
steps.instruction: Inside the Counter component, update the return statement to display the current count value from the store in a paragraph element.
steps.hint: Access the count value from the store and render it inside JSX using curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Counter component will render a paragraph showing the current count value from the persisted store.
successCriteria: The Counter component returns JSX containing a paragraph element that displays the count value from the store.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're accessing the count value from the store and rendering it inside a paragraph element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The count value isn't being displayed correctly. Check that you're accessing the store state and rendering it in JSX.

steps.title: Add increment and decrement buttons with click handlers
steps.instruction: Inside the Counter component, add two buttons: one with text 'Increment' that calls the increment action from the store, and another with text 'Decrement' that calls a new decrement action you'll need to add to the store.
steps.hint: First, add a decrement action to your store that decreases the count by 1. Then, in the Counter component, access both actions from the store and create buttons with onClick handlers that call them.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store will have both increment and decrement actions, and the Counter component will display two buttons that modify the persisted count when clicked.
successCriteria: The store includes a decrement action, the Counter component accesses both actions, and two buttons with appropriate onClick handlers are rendered.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added a decrement action to the store and both buttons with onClick handlers in the Counter component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons or click handlers are missing or incorrect. Check that you've added a decrement action to the store and properly wired both buttons to their respective actions.
